subject: Clarifications: Enclave communication paths, sidecar egress controls, and attestation artifacts
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cedarbank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cedarbank.com
Date: 2026-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI follow-up: enclave comms and egress controls

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the initial questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our infrastructure/security reviewers so we can close the network/egress sections of our RFP: 

1) Enclave communication model: please confirm which internal components initiate outbound connections (sidecar, runtime, control plane proxy) and list ports/protocols used. Is mTLS used for all inter-component traffic?

2) Egress controls: do you allow any dynamic outbound routes from runtime processes? If sidecars perform egress, what filtering (FQDN/IP allowlist) and credentialing are applied?

3) Attestation & evidence: can you provide the network diagram that maps operator control plane, dedicated pools, and customer enclaves? We also need a short artifact that shows a recent attestation manifest used for a customer proof-of-deployment.

4) Failure modes: in the event of a sidecar crash or control plane outage, what fail-open behaviors exist and how are they mitigated?

If possible, please attach a diagram and any short artifact PDFs. We are on a tight cadence to complete the security review by 3/19.

Appreciate it — Alex
Security Engineer, CedarBank

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cedarbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-11T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: enclave comms and egress controls

Alex — thanks for the specific asks. Below are concise answers and I'm attaching the diagram + evidence pack for your reviewers. If you'd like, we can jump on a 30-minute call to walk the reviewer through the diagram.

Summary answers (short):
- Initiators: sidecar proxy (per-tenant), the inference runtime (for model-sourced telemetry), and the dedicated control-plane agents for fleet orchestration.
- mTLS: enforced for all internal RPCs across internal southbound channels; control plane ⇄ sidecar uses mTLS with PKI rooted in our HSM-backed CA.
- Egress filtering: sidecars implement outbound FQDN/IP allowlists configured per-tenant (operator-managed); runtime processes do not open arbitrary outbound sockets — platform-level egress enforced at the sidecar and at host firewall.
- Fail-open: sidecar failure defaults to an operator-configurable policy. Default for hosted is "reject" (fail-close) for tenant inference traffic; for dedicated/private installs customers can opt-in to a controlled "degraded" mode with explicit risk acceptance.

Attachments included: rwi-enclave-comms-diagram-20260311.png (logical topology), egress-control-evidence-20260311.pdf (allowlist and firewall sample), attestation-manifest-20260311.json (sanitized manifest showing a recent attestation timestamp).

Detail (expanded):
1) Enclave communication model (who initiates)
- Sidecar proxy: accepts customer ingress, performs token validation, and initiates outbound connections to the runtime over mTLS for request/response and KV cache fetch. Uses TCP 443 (mutual TLS).
- Inference runtime: initiates ephemeral connections to model storage read endpoints (internal-only S3 over VPC endpoint) and telemetry sinks. These are always via VPC paths and subject to host egress rules.
- Control plane agents: scheduled orchestrator calls come from the control plane into management endpoints in the enclave over mTLS (6443-style management port equivalents). No control-plane-originated arbitrary outbound to customer networks.

2) mTLS and PKI
- All inter-component RPCs are mTLS with short-lived certs issued by an HSM-backed intermediate CA. Private deployments can bring their own PKI; we publish an attestation manifest showing cert issuance times in the attached JSON.

3) Egress controls and allowlisting
- Sidecars enforce allowlists by FQDN and IP; operator-managed deny-by-default policy. Allowlist entries are pushed via signed policy bundles and validated locally. Host firewall (iptables/nftables) enforces an additional layer: only sidecar and system services have egress ports open.

4) Failure modes and mitigations
- Sidecar crash: platform observes failure via liveness probes, immediately tears down in-flight sessions, and reports to the control plane. Default behavior is reject/new-requests; cached KV values are served only if explicitly permitted by customer policy.
- Control plane outage: routing falls back to local cached policies; long-running streaming requests may continue if the runtime already owns the session state and the customer has enabled local cache. We include a fault-mode decision matrix in the PDF.

Next steps: if reviewers want packet-level evidence or a short video walk-through, we can provide a timeboxed capture and redacted pcap under NDA.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rwi-enclave-comms-diagram-20260311.png; egress-control-evidence-20260311.pdf; attestation-manifest-20260311.json

Olga / Kim — quick internal note while we prepare the evidence pack for CedarBank: a couple items CedarBank will likely ask to see in the PDF bundle so let's confirm we have them sanitized:

- Signed policy bundle example (with FQDN allowlist entries) — we should redact any internal hostnames but keep the policy signatures intact.
- The attestation manifest: please remove any customer IDs, keep public cert serials + timestamps; indicate CA chain (redacted where necessary).
- Diagram: include a small legend showing which paths are mTLS and which are VPC-only.

Kim, can you confirm the latest host firewall snapshot (iptables output) is safe to include? If not, we should produce a sanitized sample that shows enforcement state only.

I'll draft a 1-page cover note describing 'default fail-close posture' for hosted customers and the controlled fallback option for dedicated/private customers.

- Ben
Director, Platform Security

Subject: Consolidated evidence: Enclave comms, egress controls, and attestation manifest (attachments)

Alex / CedarBank team — attaching the sanitized evidence packet we discussed. Contents at a glance:

- rwi-enclave-comms-diagram-20260311.png — logical topology: control plane, dedicated pools, sidecars, runtime, and egress filtering points. Legend indicates mTLS paths (green dashed) and VPC-only data channels (solid).
- egress-control-evidence-20260311.pdf — sample signed allowlist, host firewall enforcement snapshot (sanitized), and the fault-mode decision matrix.
- attestation-manifest-20260311.json — sanitized manifest showing cert issuance/expiry and attestation timestamp (no customer identifiers).

Responses to your numbered items:
1) Initiators and ports/protocols: sidecar (TCP 443 mTLS), runtime (internal S3 over VPC endpoints, TCP 443), control plane management (mTLS, management port).
2) mTLS: yes for all internal RPCs; HSM-backed CA; short-lived certs.
3) Dynamic outbound routes: not allowed from runtime processes; only sidecars may egress and only to allowlisted destinations; allowlists are pushed via signed bundles.
4) Fail-open behavior: hosted = default fail-close; dedicated/private = opt-in degraded mode with documented acceptance.

If your reviewers want to validate signatures on the policy bundle or inspect the JSON manifest schema, I've added a Drive link in the related_links field and can provide a time-limited verification token.

Would you prefer a 30-minute walkthrough next week (I have openings Tue/Wed afternoon PST)?

Best,
Olga Petrov
